title: page-lab/pick@1
description: One element pick, measured. The producer is scripts/lib/envelope.mjs (build) and nothing else; the consumers are the userscript-author skill and scripts/selector-verify.mjs. A consumer must never read a field this schema forbids at the envelope's fidelity: a missing candidates[].matches means UNVERIFIED, never one.
$comment: Keyword surface a dependency-free validator must implement to enforce this file: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, uniqueItems, enum, const, pattern, minLength, maxLength, minimum, allOf, anyOf, if/then, not, contains. Deliberately no $ref/$defs — every subschema is inline so the validator never resolves a pointer. No field carries serialized page markup, and additionalProperties:false is what makes that a rule rather than a wish.

schema.description: Schema identity AND version. A future shape is page-lab/pick@2 with its own file; this one is never widened in place.

status.description: picked = an element was measured. no-pick = the route ran and returned nothing usable (an html/body-terminated :hover stack, a cancelled sample). origin-mismatch = the click landed outside --expect-origin; no selector is emitted. Process-level outcomes (timeout, SIGINT, no route) exit non-zero WITHOUT an envelope.

route.description: Which tier took the measurement. Named in references/routes.md.

fidelity.description: verified = selector uniqueness confirmed by DOM.querySelectorAll against the correct scoring root, no page JS. sampled = a tool read the live DOM but scored no selectors (Kapture). asserted = passed through a sanitizer or transcribed by a human (claude-in-chrome, operator paste).

measuredAt.description: Local date of the measurement, pre-formatted for the dated WHY block hard rule 2 requires.

url.description: The URL of the document the pick came from. Always present: an envelope with no url cannot be traced to a page and is rejected (fixtures/pick-bad-no-url.json).

origin.description: Origin derived from url by the producer. The literal string "null" for opaque origins (file:, data:, sandboxed frames).

expectedOrigin.description: The --expect-origin the operator asked for. Required on status:"origin-mismatch" so the report can name both origins.

originVerified.description: true only when the measured origin was checked against an expected origin. false is legal, but then notes must carry "origin-unconfirmed" and shipBlockers the matching entry.

pageMutated.description: The act of measuring changed the DOM. True for every Kapture route: getUniqueSelector() stamps id="kapture-N" / .kapture-N. Any later HTML diff must re-measure state A.

viewport.description: The viewport the measurement was taken at. A breakpoint-sensitive selector is only meaningful with it.

tag.description: Lowercased tag name. Dashes allowed for custom elements.

id.description: The element's id attribute, empty string when it has none. A kapture-N id here is a ship blocker, not a selector.

classCount.description: How many classes the element carries. The count, not the strings, is what a report needs.

stable.description: Class fragments that survived the generated-classname heuristic and may anchor a selector.

generated.description: Class fragments that look build-generated (long, mixed-case, or a hash-shaped tail). Present here is the evidence behind a generated-classname ship blocker.

classes.description: Optional. The split is evidence for the operator, never a selector source on its own.

path.description: nth-of-type path from the scoring root. Positional and verifiable by construction: spaces and > cannot match the claude-in-chrome sanitizer's anchored regexes, and a class chain like div.card.active can.

boxes.description: DOM.getBoxModel quads, four corners as eight numbers each. Strictly more than getBoundingClientRect, and only a CDP route can produce them.

text.description: At most 200 characters of visible text, for the operator to recognise the element. Derived locally from the element's serialized markup, which is never emitted.

reachability.description: Where the node lives relative to the top document. Anything but "document" means document.querySelector in a userscript cannot reach it, and carries the matching ship blocker.

frameUrl.description: URL of the frame document the node lives in. The @match a cross-frame script needs (and it must drop @noframes).

shadowHostPath.description: Path to the shadow host from the document root. A closed root is unreachable — the pick is abandoned or re-scoped to the host.

selectorSource.description: Who produced the candidate strings. kapture-minted selectors are real, unique, and evaporate on reload — never allowed into a .user.js.

sel.description: The candidate selector, literal. Never a ${ template: a templated selector is untraceable to a measurement by construction.

matches.description: Match count from DOM.querySelectorAll against root. Present ONLY at fidelity:"verified"; its absence means unverified, never one.

root.description: What the count was taken against: "document", the shadow host path, or the frame URL. A count against the wrong root is worse than no count.

candidates.description: Three to six candidates, best first. The envelope carries every one it scored, not just the winner.

unlayeredWinner.description: An unlayered rule beats every layered rule regardless of specificity.

needsImportant.description: Whether an override actually needs !important, measured rather than assumed.

cascade.description: Optional, tier 1 only, and only when CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode / CSS.getLayersForNode were present. Evidence for the author — never a runtime dependency of the shipped script.

shipBlockers.description: Empty is the only value that lets a pick become a shipped selector. Non-empty means resolve it first — re-pick on a non-mutating route, pierce the shadow host, @match the frame, confirm the origin.

notes.description: Limitations the fidelity tier imposes, in the operator's words. Required non-empty at fidelity:"asserted", where the sanitizer or a human stands between the page and this object.

allOf.$comment: fidelity:verified — the only tier a pick may ship from. Match counts, box quads and a confirmed origin are all required; nothing is forbidden. Gated on target so a targetless envelope (status:"origin-mismatch", status:"no-pick") is not asked for evidence it deliberately does not carry; status:"picked" requires target on its own, further down. CORRECTED 2026-09-07 (found by an end-to-end run of pick-element.mjs, which refused to emit its own envelope): this branch previously also demanded originVerified===true. That conflated two ORTHOGONAL axes — fidelity describes the MEASUREMENT (CDP gave a real box and a real match count), originVerified describes whether the origin was checked against an expectation the operator supplied. A tier-1 CDP pick taken without --expect-origin is a fully verified measurement whose origin simply was not compared to anything, and it was unrepresentable. The origin rule is enforced where it belongs, by the status:"picked" branch: originVerified===true OR notes carries "origin-unconfirmed" (which lib/envelope.mjs adds, together with the ship blocker). Do not reinstate this.
fidelity:sampled — the measuring tool touched the page, so say so, pick or no pick.
fidelity:sampled — a tool read the live DOM but scored no selector. matches is FORBIDDEN: fabricating it is the drift this schema exists to stop.
fidelity:asserted — a sanitizer or a human stood between the page and this object, so the limitation must be written down.
fidelity:asserted — nothing here was scored or measured in the browser: no match counts, no box quads.
A pick must name the page it came from, and must either have had its origin checked or say out loud that it did not.
A stray click in a mail or bank tab never returns a confident envelope: both origins are named and no selector is emitted.
A Kapture-minted selector is a ship blocker by construction, enforced here and again by userscript-meta-lint.sh.
A shadow-root target cannot be reached by document.querySelector; the blocker routes the author to the host-piercing pattern.
A cross-frame target needs the frame's own @match and no @noframes.
Both walls at once, so both blockers.
